expectations.text: Recognizes the atom ('feels premium' / 'until it's great') is a taste judgment with no externally checkable signal
expectations.evidence: "its atom — 'premium / great' — is undecidable as written. There is no test, measurement, reference, or reproducible check a *separate* agent can use to pass 'this feels premium'"; Bucket C: "irreducibly subjective... 'Does this *feel* aspirational to our target buyer?' No tool and no reference-diff grounds this."

expectations.text: Does NOT immediately spin up an autonomous convergence loop against the vague goal
expectations.evidence: "So the plan is not 'here is a loop that runs until it feels premium.' The plan is: make 'premium' decidable first, then the loop is easy and safe." and "Gate verdict: As stated, undecidable — stop." Also requires confirming the brief and a dry-run of one round before spending budget.

expectations.text: Offers the honest options: build the measurement first (a concrete reference + measurable criteria like a pixel/contrast/Lighthouse rubric) OR a bounded polish pass that won't truly 'converge'
expectations.evidence: "option 1: build the missing measurement first. Buckets A+B are that measurement" (Lighthouse/axe/contrast/pixel-diff rubric) ... "option 2 is a bounded best-effort polish pass — same builders, but it stops on the round cap, not an earned bar, and I will label the output 'polished,' not 'converged.'"

expectations.text: Explains WHY looping on an unmeasurable target fails (drift, reward-hacking / gaming its own judgment, burns budget without direction)
expectations.evidence: "an autonomous loop pointed straight at it would do exactly what ungrounded loops always do: drift, congratulate itself, and burn a large budget polishing taste before declaring a green 'great' it never earned." and "self-critique with no external signal flips correct work to wrong more than the reverse."
